why: Machines are rooms and tasks are meetings: the minimum number of machines is the maximum number of tasks active at the same moment. It is Meeting Rooms II with one twist, inclusive end times.
hints: How many tasks are running at the busiest instant? You can never use fewer machines than that.
The answer is the peak overlap. Because both ends are inclusive, a task ending at 7 and one starting at 7 overlap and need different machines.
Sort by start and keep a min-heap of end times; pop while heap top < current start (strictly), then push. Or sweep events with +1 at start and -1 at end+1. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Endpoints are inclusive: (1,7) and (6,7) overlap, and so do (3,6) and (6,7). Pop only ends strictly less than the new start.
Identical tasks (example with four copies of [2,5]) each need their own machine.
n is up to 2*10^5, so the O(n^2) pairwise check is too slow.
